planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in a large patio pot or small trellis bed; this compact Boulevard Collection selection is bred for small-space gardens rather than covering a large structure.

directions: Corinne is part of Raymond Evison's compact Boulevard Collection, bred for container and small-garden use on a trellis, obelisk, or patio pot rather than a large structure. Its ruffled white blooms, roughly 4 inches across, carry a pale pink central stripe that deepens near a smoky red-grey center, opening in late spring and again through summer into autumn. Because it flowers on both old and new growth, trim lightly after the first flush and cut back to about 12-18 inches in early spring to keep it tidy and encourage the next round of bloom. Give it full sun with the root zone kept cool and shaded, as with other large-flowered hybrids.

planting.note: Plant in spring in a large container or small trellis bed in moist, well-drained soil; this Boulevard Collection selection stays compact enough for a patio but still needs firm support.

directions: Vicki is a compact Boulevard Collection selection bred for patio containers and small trellises, staying low and narrow rather than sprawling. Large, ruffled pink flowers 4-5 inches across show a deeper pink central bar and a bright boss of golden-yellow stamens, opening from early summer and repeating into early autumn. As a group 3 clematis it blooms entirely on the current season's growth, so cut all stems back hard to roughly a foot above the soil in late winter or early spring. It performs best in moist, well-drained, neutral to alkaline soil in full sun to light shade.

planting.note: Plant in spring in a patio container or small bed; Kitty was introduced for the Chelsea Flower Show as one of the most compact Boulevard Collection selections and suits a deck railing or balcony.

directions: Kitty is one of the most compact members of the Boulevard Collection, bred small enough for a single large patio pot and first launched at the Chelsea Flower Show. Its near-white flowers open in two distinct flushes, first in early to midsummer and again in late summer into autumn, smothering the modest 2.5-4 foot vine. It flowers only on new wood, so cut all growth back hard to around 6 inches in late winter or early spring to reset it for the coming season. Its small stature and tolerance of container culture make it an easy choice where space is limited.

planting.note: Plant in spring in a large container or small trellis bed; this Boulevard Collection selection stays compact and is noted for being largely untroubled by deer and rabbits.

directions: Edda is a Boulevard Collection selection grown for its unusually dark, semi-double flowers: deep purple, overlapping sepals edged with fine red-violet pinstripes surround a pale central boss of stamens. Blooms open from late spring into summer with a second flush in early autumn on a compact, bushy climber only 3-4 feet tall, well suited to a large container or small trellis. Like other patio clematis in the series it flowers on new growth, so prune hard each year to healthy buds about a foot above the ground in early spring. It is largely untroubled by deer and rabbits and draws pollinators readily to its distinctive striped blooms.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring against a sheltered, sunny wall or fence; this evergreen Armand clematis selection needs a warm microclimate in the colder parts of its range to set flower buds reliably.

directions: Snow Bells is an evergreen Armand clematis selection raised in the Netherlands from two unnamed white-flowered Clematis armandii parents and later patented in the US for its fragrance and bloom quality. In late winter, nodding, bell-shaped, greenish-white flowers open along the previous year's stems and release a strong, sweet scent often compared to Daphne odora, with individual blooms lasting about ten days. Its narrow, glossy, leathery leaves stay handsome year-round on a vigorous, upright climber best trained on a sheltered, sunny wall or fence in mild-winter regions. Because flower buds form on old wood, prune only right after flowering to control size, never in late winter.
